proposals.argument: The DRBD board's fsx FAIL of 2026-10-21T19:36:37Z (dry-run candidate 0.90.133-2, build 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A, seed=3832054505, both checks failed in 2 s of an 88 s budget) is the detector failing, not MeshXFS. tests/suite/fsx.sh drew its seed from four random bytes (0..2^32-1); the vendored fsx keeps -S in an int (tests/suite/tools/fsx.c:186 'int seed = 1;', :3397 getnum) and calls usage() for a negative value (:3402-3403), exiting 90 before any operation, so neither check ran a single fsx operation on the filesystem. Reproduced host-local with the same binary: -S 3832054505 and -S 2147483648 exit 90 with the usage line; -S 2147483647 and -S 1 run (rc=0). The old draw put 10022 of 20000 seeds above INT_MAX. The detector fix is in the tree: tests/suite/fsx.sh now draws 1..2^31-1 (20000 draws, none outside) and keeps a failing check's fsx log on the node with its path in the record instead of deleting it. Nothing in the run is evidence about MeshXFS either way: fsx never opened its file.

Resubmission of P20261021-4bb0fe, which was rejected (data/reviews/P20261021-4bb0fe.md) on three points, answered here. The run: the DRBD board's fsx FAIL of 2026-10-21T19:36:37Z (dry-run candidate 0.90.133-2, build 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A, seed=3832054505, both checks failed in 2 s of 88 s) is the detector failing, not MeshXFS: tests/suite/fsx.sh drew its seed from 0..2^32-1, the vendored fsx keeps -S in an int (tests/suite/tools/fsx.c:186, :3397) and calls usage(), exit 90, for a negative value (:3402-3403) before it opens its file (:3493), so neither check ran an fsx operation. Reproduced host-local with the same binary (tests/evidence/fsx_seed_int_max_repro_20261021.log). (1) THE FIXED DETECTOR HAS PASSED THERE: tests/evidence/drbd_rig/criteria.runs.jsonl line 3230, 2/net/mesh/drbd fsx 2026-10-21T20:57:33Z PASS 'checks=2 passed=2 failed=0 seed=1472941388', 14 s of 88 s, run 20261021T205705Z-g2, same build 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A, on the fixed fsx.sh. (2) THE FIX, NAMED: the tree is uncommitted (the owner has not yet directed a commit; this session may not commit unasked), so the change is named by a hashed diff, tests/evidence/fsx_seed_fix_20261021.diff: the seed line becomes '% 2147483647 + 1' (1..2^31-1; 20000 draws, none outside, in the repro log), and a failing check keeps its log at /root/fsx.<seed>.<ops>.log on the node with fsx_fail_log=<host>:<path> in the run's measured field and its tail in the kernel log, instead of the old /tmp file the EXIT trap deleted. On the record's own next step (logs under the run's evidence): the node's log stays where the run names it; run.sh copying it into tests/evidence is not part of this fix. (3) THE RECORD: D-FSX-RANDOM-SEED-ABOVE-INT-MAX-MAKES-FSX-EXIT-WITH-USAGE-AND-LOGS-ARE-DELETED names this run in its cells; a detector-defect proposal carries no --record (tools/defects.py takes a record only for record proposals), so it is named here.

The owner was asked (2026-10-22, recorded verbatim as the last owner_approved entry of data/release_policy.json) to choose between approving an exception for this record in data/release_policy.json and holding 0.90.134 for the IPMI fence work. The owner answered 'leave the DRBD work for .135/.136': 0.90.134 does not wait for the DRBD fence work, so the record is excepted for 0.90.134 at 2/net/mesh/drbd only, the configuration it reaches. The policy's exceptions entry names exactly this record, 2/net/mesh/drbd and release 0.90.134. Nothing else about the record changes: it stays open with impact stability, reach 2 nodes */*/drbd, its evidence and its next step, and it blocks 2/net/mesh/drbd in every other release (tools/defects.py owner_exception and excepted_here: an excepted_at mark counts only for its candidate and only while the policy still grants it).

The release build step of the 0.90.133-2 dry run failed before building anything: its whole-tree rsync could not read a root-only result file, tests/evidence/candidates/0.90.133-2.build.log:2 'rsync: [sender] send_files failed to open "/home/steve/src/mxfs/bench.json": Permission denied (13)', :4 '=== rc=23', recorded as data/criteria.runs.jsonl:6836 'could not copy the tree'. That is the step's own fault (the detector): bench.json is a benchmark result, not a frozen input, and nothing about the candidate's module or tools was measured. The detector fix is in the tree: tools/release_run.py:229-238, the build copies the candidate's frozen file list only (rsync --files-from of the manifest's files), with the comment naming this failure; CHANGELOG.md 0.90.133 entry, 'The clean build copied the whole tree and stopped on a root-only result file. It now copies the candidate's frozen file list and nothing else'. Independent evidence that the candidate built: the next build step on the same module 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A passed on the fixed detector (data/criteria.runs.jsonl:6943, 2026-10-21T20:49:59Z, 'clean build 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A, tools, tauth, audits'), and every build step since passed (:6962, :7053, :7144). Collected in tests/evidence/incident_remaining_evidence_20261023.txt:2701-2718.

The packages step of the 0.90.133-2 dry run failed in the platform build check, before any package was built, because the rig's Proxmox build VM lacked the kernel headers for one claimed kernel: tests/evidence/candidates/0.90.133-2.packages.log:10 'VM_KBUILD_FAIL pve9 pve9-1 7.0.14-24-pve (no headers for 7.0.14-24-pve installed on pve9-1)', :11 'NO_HEADERS 7.0.14-24-pve', :12 'ERROR: ... failed; no packages built' (scripts/vm_kbuild_check.sh:74 prints NO_HEADERS when the VM has no $hdr/Makefile for that kernel, :91). The same check built MeshXFS on that VM for the other kernels in the same step (:6 VM_KBUILD_OK ... 7.0.14-19-pve, :8 VM_KBUILD_OK ... 6.17.2-1-pve), so the build itself was sound; the missing header package is the VM's state, outside MeshXFS, and it precedes the failure. Once the headers were on the VM the identical check passed for that kernel: tests/evidence/candidates/0.90.134_20261021T212712Z.packages.log:6 'VM_KBUILD_OK pve9 pve9-1 7.0.14-24-pve C0589CD3CE0FFA63297F6A8' (2026-10-21T21:27Z) and 0.90.134_20261021T230333Z.packages.log:6, and the packages step passed at data/criteria.runs.jsonl:7055 (2026-10-21T23:30:01Z, '3 packages in dist/0.90.134'). No MeshXFS kernel line is involved: nothing was loaded or mounted in this step. Collected in tests/evidence/incident_remaining_evidence_20261023.txt:2719-2743.

The platforms step of the 0.90.133-2 dry run had no packages to verify, because the packages step before it had failed on the build VM's missing kernel headers (tests/evidence/candidates/0.90.133-2.packages.log:10-12, 'VM_KBUILD_FAIL pve9 pve9-1 7.0.14-24-pve (no headers for 7.0.14-24-pve installed on pve9-1)' ... 'no packages built'; data/candidates/0.90.133-2.json:46-52 packages failed). tests/full_verify.sh then refused before running a round: tests/evidence/candidates/0.90.133-2.platforms.log:2 'PLATFORMS leaves out pve9, which has no run of 0.90.133-2 to be graded on', :3 '=== rc=2', recorded as data/criteria.runs.jsonl:6911 'full_verify platforms rc=2, -1 failed step(s)'. No package was installed and no node ran MeshXFS in this step, so it measured nothing of MeshXFS; its cause is the same infrastructure fault, outside MeshXFS, that preceded it. The step now refuses outright when the packages step did not pass (tools/release_run.py:489-493, comment naming 0.90.133-2), and with packages present it passed: data/criteria.runs.jsonl:7129 (2026-10-22T01:55:36Z, "every released platform's packaged round and hung-node test"). proposals.argument: FIXED AND VERIFIED. The cause: tools/release_run.py records each step's outcome as a ledger run keyed config '1/any' (or the step's configuration) and row 'release:<step>'; no disposition can settle a failed one, so the first step that fails on any candidate leaves an incident the gate can never clear. Reproducer: tests/release_step_cell_lap.py (host only, under 1 s): takes a recorded release step FAIL from the primary ledger and requires it to parse as a cell (tools/criteria.py parse_cell), to be found in the ledger and to take an annotation; prints EXPOSED for the recorded step FAIL it uses. With the fix taken out parse_cell refuses the step's key ('criteria: 1/any: wanted <nodes>/<class>/<method>/<attach>'): STEP_CELL_LAP FAIL Control b20261022-3f5a50: with the fix taken out (fix reverted: tests/evidence/controls/D-RELEASE-RUN-STEP-INCIDENTS-CANNOT-BE-SETTLED.fix.diff sha256=d047663cb6c5df48da3dfdf0c4ed479b9fc43e646644a4f28d920324a57cd688) 20 of 20 laps failed (tests/evidence/batch_laps/b20261022-3f5a50/), each lap failing on the cause itself as the reproducer describes. Fix-on batch b20261022-332c20, sized from that control (plan-verify --control b20261022-3f5a50): 4 of 4 laps PASS with exposure on the frozen candidate 0.90.134. Laps: tests/evidence/lanes/host_verify_round1_20261023T022524Z/step1.log lists laps 1..4, each 'PASS ... exposure=N' with N>=1; the batch's laps and their logs are in tests/evidence/batch_laps/b20261022-332c20/ and in the primary ledger (data/criteria.runs.jsonl, row lap:release_step_cell at 2/net/mesh/direct, batch b20261022-332c20), every one with candidate 0.90.134 and build 16A5F5DDDB4852C9D5DB236.

change.cause: chk_mxfs repair rebuilds an AG free-space btrees (rebuild_freespace_btrees, called from check_freespace_btrees when the AG has btree errors and agi_count == 0) as one extent from block 8 to the end of the AG. Three kinds of owned block fall inside it: (1) block 8 is the fourth AGFL block on the layout mkfs writes at 512 (mkfs_mxfs.c calc_ag_layout: roots 1-4, AGFL 5-8, free from 9); (2) on the log AG the log starts at block 5, so the whole log is declared free; (3) agi_count == 0 means no inode chunk in the AG, not no data: extents of files whose inodes live in other AGs are declared free. Any allocation afterwards can give one of those blocks a second owner.

change.cause: chk_mxfs repair rebuilds an AG free-space btrees (rebuild_freespace_btrees, called from check_freespace_btrees when the AG has btree errors and agi_count == 0) as one extent from block 8 to the end of the AG. Three kinds of owned block fall inside it: (1) block 8 is the fourth AGFL block on the layout mkfs writes at 512 (mkfs_mxfs.c calc_ag_layout: roots 1-4, AGFL 5-8, free from 9); (2) on the log AG the log starts at block 5, so the whole log is declared free; (3) agi_count == 0 means no inode chunk in the AG, not no data: extents of files whose inodes live in other AGs are declared free. proposals.argument: FIXED AND VERIFIED. The cause: On 8/net/mesh/mpath, in the one-path phase of path_peer_withdrawn, after the second withdrawn peer was fenced and recovered and test21 took over its authority-ledger pages, test21's ledger refused 110 conflicting AG 6 EX grants to another survivor in six seconds (P-TAUTH-DOUBLE-GRANT ... vs record ex=<test21>), then test21 received a fresh CAW grant on AG 6 whose lineage was still open (P130-FALSE-FRESH), refused it as in-memory corruption and shut its filesystem down: a survivor of a clean peer departure crashed out of the cluster. Reproducer: tests/tauth/adopted_grant_handoff_test.sh reproduces it in one process with four nodes: C holds EX on R, mastered by B; A's wait times out into the TEST ONLY gap (dl_acq_gap_ino/dl_acq_gap_ms); C releases and B's grant is adopted; D leaves, and R's page is handed from B to A; A's next attempt is answered by the already-granted shortcut. Exposure is the test's line that the grant was adopted, the page handed and the shortcut taken locally ('EXPOSURE adopted=1 handed=1 local=1'). With the fix taken out A held EX with no entry in its own table, B's EX was refused by A's ledger as a double grant, and R stayed refused after A's unlock; with it in, A's master keeps A's EX and B is granted after A's release. proposals.argument: FIXED AND VERIFIED. The cause: tests/fourkn_merge_2node.sh holds each node's first 64 merged inode-block writes 20 ms between the read and the COMPARE AND WRITE so a peer's write of the same block lands in between, but it lands only in most laps: of 4 held laps on the 4K-native LUN, 1 saw no MISCOMPARE and exited VACUOUS, so one lap does not reliably exercise the merged write's retry Reproducer: the board row fourkn_merge (tests/suite/fourkn_merge.sh, test31/test32 on the 4096-byte pool LUN) runs its workload unheld, and at the unmount node 1 holds its one merged write of a block between the read and the swap while node 2 writes its own slot of the same block; node 1's swap then miscompares and its retry must keep node 2's slot. Exposure is the row's forced overlap landing (forced=landed, miscompares>=1, exposure=1 in the run's measured line). With the overlap switched off the row is the old unforced lap, which retried no MISCOMPARE in most laps (VACUOUS, graded FAIL). change.cause: tests/suite/fsx.sh drew its seed from 4 random bytes (0..2^32-1); the vendored fsx keeps -S in an int (tests/suite/tools/fsx.c:186) and calls usage() for a negative value (:3402-3403), which exits 90 (:2745), so a draw above INT_MAX (about half of all draws) made fsx exit at once and the row record a FAIL that exercised nothing.

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

THE CAUSE, MEASURED. (1) Code: tests/suite/tools/fsx.c:186 'int seed = 1;', :3397 'seed = getnum(optarg, &endp);', :3402-3403 'if (seed < 0) usage();', and usage() (:2654) ends :2745 'exit(90);'. (2) The vendored binary itself, tests/suite/tools/fsx, sha256 2e740285ca706ac94609964e3626c28352a60341e05c4994e7e89d31cabfca1a, ctime 2026-10-14 (unchanged since; the review P20261022-b2613a check 2 records the same ctime): tests/evidence/fsx_seed_int_max_repro_20261021.log (its header names the binary by the first 16 hex digits of that hash) gives seed=3832054505 rc=90 and seed=2147483648 rc=90, each with first line 'usage: fsx [...]', and seed=2147483647 rc=0 and seed=1 rc=0, 'Seed set to ...'; the old draw (od -N4 -tu4) put 10022 of 20000 draws above INT_MAX, the fixed draw 0 of 20000 outside 1..2147483647. tests/evidence/fsx_seed_4294967295_repro_20261023T062142Z.log measures the very seed the control forced: seed=4294967295 rc=90 'usage: fsx [...]' (4294967295 as an int is -1), seed=2147483647 rc=0. (3) The approved detector-defect review data/reviews/P20261021-676432.md established the same mechanism for the board run 2/net/mesh/drbd:fsx:2026-10-21T19:36:37Z (fsx rejects the negative seed during option parsing, before it opens its file).

THE FIX: tests/suite/fsx.sh:30 SEED="${FSX_SEED:-$(( $(od -An -N4 -tu4 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n') % 2147483647 + 1 ))}", always 1..2147483647; the diff is tests/evidence/controls/D-FSX-RANDOM-SEED-ABOVE-INT-MAX.fix.diff, sha256 8696fceaa6c7370480148efe459b824c241407ac3fda6c037ac4e664782ea61f, one hunk, the SEED= line.

REPRODUCER: tests/fsx_seed_lap.sh binds four 0xff bytes over /dev/urandom in a private mount namespace and runs fsx.sh on tmpfs, so the draw is 4294967295 in every lap. With the fix out fsx.sh passes -S 4294967295; with it in, the fixed line maps that draw to 2.

change.cause: tests/lib/rig.sh could not resolve an EUI-64 LUN by its identifier: mxfs_wwid_norm stripped naa., 0x and mpath- but not eui., so eui.<hex> became e<hex>, and the no-mount fallback looked only for /dev/disk/by-id/wwn-0x<decl>, a link udev never makes for an EUI-64 designator (it makes scsi-2<hex>).

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

THE CAUSE, MEASURED IN THE CONTROL'S OWN LAPS. Every logged control lap prints the pool LUN's identifier and the links the resolver then looked for, e.g. tests/evidence/batch_laps/b20261022-bf8f03/20261022T202059Z.log:2 "INFO test29 sda wwid='eui.3837303435343634' mxfs mounts=0", :3 "EXPOSED: test29's pool LUN is EUI-64 (eui.3837303435343634)", :4 "ABORT: no MXFS device basis on test29: no MXFS_DEV, no live mxfs mount, no /dev/disk/by-id/{wwn-0x,scsi-3,scsi-2}e3837303435343634, no MXFS_CONFIG": the identifier normalised with its stray 'e' (eui. stripped as if it were 'eui' followed by a hex string beginning e), so no by-id link of any designator type could match. The fix-on laps resolve the same LUN on the same node through the link udev does make: tests/evidence/batch_laps/b20261022-8cd6d2/20261023T040335Z-cc02c49e.log:5 'DEVICE node=test29 path=/dev/disk/by-id/scsi-23837303435343634 source=declared-wwid wwid=eui.3837303435343634'.

THE FIX: tests/lib/rig.sh normalises eui. like naa., and the no-mount fallback tries the by-id links udev makes for each designator type (wwn-0x and scsi-3 for NAA, scsi-2 for EUI-64); tests/rig_lib_contract.sh 11b, 13b and 13h accept either designator. The diff is tests/evidence/controls/D-RIG-LIB-EUI64-LUN-ID-NORMALISED-WITH-STRAY-E.fix.diff, sha256 62c688f79bff83a4525b140807cc3f5b222a0ab436a1ef2e1466dea7370332cf; it changes one file, tests/lib/rig.sh.

REPRODUCER: tests/rig_eui64_resolve_lap.sh <node1>,<node2> <group>, on a pool pair whose LUN is EUI-64 with no mxfs mount on the node: it sources tests/lib/rig.sh (:33) and resolves the pair's LUN by its identifier as the capture-gate entries do. EXPOSED is printed only when the node's LUN wwid is eui.*; PASS needs source=declared-wwid.

change.cause: scripts/rig_lane.sh released a lane's configuration locks only through each holder's 1 s poll of the lane's pid (tail --pid), so for up to a second after a lane ended a lane started on the same configuration was refused as if the ended lane still ran; the lane's EXIT trap now kills and waits for every holder (release_holds), so the locks are free before its exit is seen

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED. The defect: scripts/rig_lane.sh held each configuration a lane names with a holder process (`tail --pid=$$ -f /dev/null`, scripts/rig_lane.sh:77) that sees the lane's exit only at its next 1 s poll, so for up to a second after a lane ended its configuration lock (/tmp/mxfs_lane.<configuration>.lock, flock -n at :70-71) was still held, and a lane started in that second on the same configuration was refused (rc 3) as if the ended lane still ran.

The fix (one site): the lane records each holder's pid (HOLDERS, :57 and :78) and its EXIT trap release_holds (:58-66) kills and waits for every holder, so the locks are free before the lane's exit can be seen. LANE_HOLD_RELEASE=0 makes release_holds return at once (:59), leaving the release to the holder's poll alone, which is the behaviour before the fix; recording the pids changes nothing else.

Cause, instrumented: the reproducer tests/lane_config_lock_lap.sh starts lane A (holds 64/net/mesh/direct 4 s), lane B while A runs (must be refused) and lane C the moment A's process has exited, and prints 'EXPOSED-RELEASE: lane C was started N ms after lane A exited' (N under the holder's 1 s poll) on every lap.

change.cause: the bmbt write chokepoint at bio submit (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c, the mxfs_buf_xfsaild_skip_bmbt_write test in the submit path) judged read bios as well as writes, reading the owner from the buffer's in-memory image; for a buffer an eviction had cleared of XBF_DONE, whose memory still held a deleted file's extent-tree leaf whose owner number had become a directory this node holds NL, it skipped the READ of the reused block: mxfs_bmbt_skip_preserve_truth staled the buffer and xfs_buf_ioend verified the old image and set XBF_DONE, so the reader was handed the other tree's leaf; the chokepoint now judges writes only (mxfs_bmbt_chokepoint_covers) and every read is issued

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: on 2/net/mesh/direct test1 read 2 of 8 files its peer had just written and fsynced and got no data. Its buffer cache served extent-tree (bmbt) leaves still carrying the owner of a file from the previous lap, deleted and its blocks reused for the new files' trees; the btree owner check refused them (P975-BMBT-LOOKUP-BAD same_image=0 flags=0x60) and the reads failed.

The cause, proven: the bmbt write chokepoint in the bio submit path had no direction test. For a read of a block whose buffer had been evicted (XBF_DONE cleared) but still held the old leaf in memory, the owner it read from that memory had become a directory test1 holds NL, so the predicate said skip: mxfs_bmbt_skip_preserve_truth read the LUN, found it different (P77-SKIP-DIFFERS same=0) and staled the buffer, the chokepoint printed P61-CHOKEPOINT-SKIP-BMBT and completed the bio with xfs_buf_ioend and no I/O, which for an XBF_READ buffer verifies the old image and sets XBF_DONE. The lookup then got the old leaf with XBF_DONE|XBF_STALE (0x60), exactly as P975 printed. Instrumented before the fix: lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2_bmbt_openefi_diag_20261023T072311Z (MXFS_EXTRA_MODARGS=bmbt_skip_reads=1, the old behaviour, which printed the direction): every P975 followed a P61-CHOKEPOINT-READ of the same daddr ('skipped, the old image is served with no read'), and 3 of 12 open-EFI laps failed.

The fix (one site): mxfs_bmbt_chokepoint_covers (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c:8840-8874), called at the chokepoint (:9692-9693), returns true for a write and, for a read, the knob bmbt_skip_reads (default 0): a read is always issued. bmbt_skip_reads=1 makes the chokepoint skip a matched read exactly as before the fix, since covers() is the chokepoint's only added condition; the function also counts each matched read (bmbt_chokepoint_reads), the lap's exposure. The readahead hold dbg_bmbt_ra_hold_ms (default 0) is test instrumentation, set to 300 ms in both arms so the synchronous read meets the readahead's buffer every time.

The gate lap 2/net/mesh/direct:gate:d_intents_2tcp_open_efi:2026-10-23T06:20:27Z (lap 7 of b20261023-b40448, build 16A5F5DDDB4852C9D5DB236, whose chokepoint printed every skip as a write) shows the same sequence in tests/evidence/20261023T061841Z_intents2tcp_openefivc7-d_intents_2tcp_open_efi-ok/dmesg_test1.txt: :248 and :250 'P61-CHOKEPOINT-SKIP-BMBT owner=2097287 daddr=2106984', then :251 'P975-BMBT-LOOKUP-BAD daddr=2106984 want_ino=2097296 ... cached_owner=2097287 ... flags=0x60 ... same_image=0'; :294 and :296 the skips of daddr=2164704 (owner 2097290), then :297 its P975 (want_ino=2097298) and the corruption report :298; no node wrote either block on test1 (they are the peer's new trees' leaves, owner directory NL here), so each skipped bio was the lookup's read. The directory-block skip later in the same function (mxfs_buf_xfsaild_skip_dir_write, :9750, :9971) has no direction test either, but every switch that lets it complete a bio without I/O is off by default (mxfs_dirskip_enabled, xfs/xfs_mxfs_debug.c:916; mxfs_dir_reflush_skip, xfs/xfs_mxfs_buf.c:118; mxfs_dir_tenure_reflush_skip, :139; mxfs_dir_relepoch_skip, xfs/xfs_mxfs_debug.c:991) and neither the rig nor the packages set one, so as shipped it never serves a read; it is not this record's cause or fix.

FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: tests/tauth/Makefile's rules for the five shared objects list some of the headers each source includes and not others (tests/tauth/Makefile:131-132 dlm_shared.o lists only dlm/dlm_shared.c; :146-147 and :149-150 tauth_store.o and tauth_ledger.o omit pal/pal.h and dlm/dlm.h). The fix, every site:
- tests/tauth/shared_objs.sh:15-35, tauth_shared_objs <top> <outdir>: compiles the five from clean into the caller's directory with the Makefile's flags (:27-32) and prints their paths. TAUTH_SHARED_FROM_CLEAN=0 (:18-24) runs the plain make in tests/tauth as before the fix, the same-build control.

The defect: when one rank of the alloc_witness row aborted its own precondition, the other rank waited for it until the row's 120 s budget killed both, and the board recorded FAIL BUDGET_EXHAUSTED on both ranks instead of the abort that ended the lap.

AW_ABORT_BROADCAST=0 restores both pre-fix paths exactly: fail_out goes to the final rendezvous (:163) and aw_barrier is the plain coord_barrier (:174-176). This record's census half (the script wrote no mxfs-CCph phase marker) was split into D-ALLOC-WITNESS-WROTE-NO-PHASE-MARKER-SO-A-TIMED-OUT-ROW-CENSUS-READS-NONE, which stays open: this removal claims only the abort broadcast, the one fix its control turns off.

change.cause: tests/live_holder_wait.sh made its eight candidate inodes back to back, so their numbers were consecutive, and under ledger routing version 2 an inode routes with the low three bits of its number cleared (MXFS_TAUTH_INO_SHARD): the eight were one or two routing shards and so one or two mastership draws, and on a formation where those drew H itself none was remote-mastered from W and the harness aborted before measuring; H now creates objects until 16 distinct routing shards are represented and keeps the first in each as a candidate

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: tests/live_holder_wait.sh aborts before measuring ('ABORT: none of the eight candidates is remote-mastered from test2') when none of its candidates is mastered by the other node. It made its eight candidates back to back, so they were consecutive inode numbers.

The cause, from the routing code: a resource's master is active_nodes[page % N] (dlm/dlm.c:2445-2454), where page is its routing hash modulo the page count (dlm/dlm.c:2436-2443), and for an inode under routing version 2 the hash is taken with the low MXFS_TAUTH_INO_SHARD_BITS (3) of the number cleared (include/mxfs/mxfs_tauth.h:131-132, :498-508). So all eight inodes of one aligned group of eight share one master: eight consecutive numbers are one or two draws, and whenever those landed on H the lap could not run. Measured on the dry-run attempt's gate: candidates 8389321-8389328, all local.

The fix, one site: tests/live_holder_wait.sh:311-370. H creates objects (at most 160) until 16 distinct shards (ino >> 3) are represented, keeps the first object in each as a candidate, and removes the spares only after every candidate exists, since a freed number is taken by the next create and would draw the same shard again (:322-328, :339, :352-363). Each candidate is then its own draw: different shard numbers hash to independent pages through the hash's final avalanche (include/mxfs/mxfs_tauth.h:471-475), so on two nodes all 16 land on H with probability 2^-16, where the eight consecutive candidates did with probability 1/2 or 1/4. In that case the harness still refuses with its ABORT line, the honest answer for a formation it cannot measure, never a measurement of the wrong path. LH_SHARD_SELECT=0 (:335-337) keeps eight objects back to back, all of them, as before the fix: the same-build control.

change.cause: A clean last-member unmount's release-all (dlm_wire_release_all in dlm/dlm.c, reached from mxfs_dlm_release_all at dlm/v5_mount.c:22458) released every grant the member held one authority-ledger transition at a time, each about 0.9 ms of page commit under mxfs_tauth_page_write (FUA reads, COMPARE AND WRITE writes, flushes), serially, so a last member holding 32000-40000 grants took 28-61 s to unmount, over the 30 s stall limit.

proposals.argument: FIXED AND VERIFIED. Cause, measured (lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2_lmu_trace_20261023T075544Z, build B155E10D900872E6CE36289): A's unmount 30972 and 31746 ms at NFILES=32000, of which release-all took 27939 and 28708 ms releasing 31946 and 31962 grants (tests/evidence/20261023T075654Z_lmutrace_lmu32k1/a_kmsg.txt 'P-RELALL-WALL released=31946 ms=27939', tests/evidence/20261023T080029Z_lmutrace_lmu32k2 'released=31962 ms=28708'); the umount task's stack samples taken every 200 ms are FUA reads, COMPARE AND WRITE writes and flushes under mxfs_tauth_page_write; at NFILES=4000 'released=4001 ms=3684'. The wall is the grant count times one page commit. Fix: dlm_wire_release_all sends the remote masters' releases first on its own thread and commits the locally mastered ones on dl_relall_threads threads (default 8, each taking every nth resource); dl_relall_threads=1 is the old serial release-all, so the knob takes exactly the fix out on the same build. Precheck lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2_relall_prechecks_20261023T080727Z: 8 threads against 1 on the same formation. Control b20261023-9a3afc (tests/evidence/lanes/g2_attempt1011_20261023T101421Z/step13.log): candidate 0.90.134's module 08D63764A9352FBDD5A76CD on the g2 pair, dl_relall_threads=1 through MXFS_EXTRA_MODARGS on each lap's own prep, tests/last_member_umount_lap.sh at its default nfiles=40000 (the verify review's correction: not 32000; both batches ran the same value): 10 of 10 exposed laps FAIL, A's last-member unmount 37573-61378 ms against 30000. Verification b20261023-dff6ea (tests/evidence/lanes/g2_attempt1011_20261023T101421Z/step14.log), sized from it (L=0.5887, N=6), the same build, lap, pair and nfiles with the default 8 threads: 6 of 6 exposed laps PASS, 10256-12906 ms; approved and applied (P20261023-8226ea, data/reviews/P20261023-8226ea.md: every lap sv=08D63764A9352FBDD5A76CD, KNOB=8, A's kernel log shows each release-all handling 39842-39938 grants). Every run this record names is a control lap of b20261023-9a3afc (its cells), settled by that verification. Scope: the path runs only under the TCP lock manager: ctx->dlm is the TCP DLM, created on the TCP path (dlm/v5_mount.c:20534, 'TCP DLM create failed' on error), and the unmount calls mxfs_dlm_release_all only when ctx->dlm is set (:22457-22458); a COMPARE AND WRITE mount releases through mxfs_dlm_caw_stop (:22453-22455) and opens no authority ledger (tauth_open, :21070), so disk/caw configurations never run the serial release-all. On net/mesh configurations the wall is per grant the last member holds (the measured 0.9 ms per page commit, 28 s at 32000 against 3.7 s at 4000), not per node or attachment: the fix divides the locally mastered commits over 8 threads and moves remote masters' releases off them whatever the node count. change.cause: tests/tooling/alloc_witness.sh: a rank that aborted its own precondition wrote ABORT to its rank file and then waited at the final rendezvous while its peer waited at the next one; both waits are bounded by COORD_TIMEOUT, which run.sh passes at its default of 120 s, equal to the row's 120 s budget, so both ran until the budget killed them (rc=124) and the board recorded BUDGET_EXHAUSTED on both ranks with the abort nowhere in it; an aborting rank now broadcasts its abort (coord_signal_abort) and every rendezvous returns the moment one has (aw_barrier), so the peer records ABORTED_BY_PEER with the reason and the row ends at once

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: when one rank of the alloc_witness row aborted its own precondition, the other rank waited for it until the row's 120 s budget killed both, and the board recorded FAIL BUDGET_EXHAUSTED on both ranks instead of the abort that ended the lap.

The fix, one file: tests/tooling/alloc_witness.sh:148-194. fail_out (:158-167) records the abort and, with AW_ABORT_BROADCAST=1 (the default, :157), broadcasts it through the row's coordination channel (coord_signal_abort, tests/suite/coord.sh:182-193, which predates the fix and dir_reuse_coherency.sh already uses); peer_out (:168-172) records ABORTED_BY_PEER with the aborting rank's reason; aw_barrier (:173-194) runs each rendezvous in the background and returns 2 the moment coord_check_abort sees a peer's abort. AW_ABORT_BROADCAST=0 restores both pre-fix paths exactly: fail_out goes to the final rendezvous (:163) and aw_barrier is the plain coord_barrier (:174-176). Both waits are bounded by COORD_TIMEOUT, which run.sh passes at its default of 120 s (run.sh:307, :1658, :1883); that equals the row's 120 s manifest budget (tests/tooling/manifest:25) but is not derived from it, so the comment at alloc_witness.sh:150-151 ('hands a row its whole budget as COORD_TIMEOUT') overstates the link; what ends both ranks is the measured rc=124 at 120 s. This record's census half (the script wrote no mxfs-CCph phase marker) was split into D-ALLOC-WITNESS-WROTE-NO-PHASE-MARKER-SO-A-TIMED-OUT-ROW-CENSUS-READS-NONE, which stays open: this removal claims only the abort broadcast, the one fix its control turns off.

change.cause: tests/suite/fourkn_merge.sh held each node's first merged inode-block writes between the read and the COMPARE AND WRITE until the peer's swap of the block landed, but nothing made the peer write that block inside the hold, so a lap with no MISCOMPARE retried exited VACUOUS; the row now runs its workload unheld and forces the overlap once a lap at the unmount (node 1 holds its one merged write of a block while node 2 writes its own slot of that block and unmounts), so node 1's swap miscompares and retries in every lap, and a lap where that does not land is VACUOUS

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: tests/suite/fourkn_merge.sh, the 4K-native boards' merged-write row, waited for an overlap it never made. It held each node's first merged inode-block writes between the read and the COMPARE AND WRITE (hold=8x1000ms: up to 1000 ms each, until the peer's swap of the block lands), but nothing made the peer write that block inside the hold, so a lap with no MISCOMPARE retried exited VACUOUS. The row's requirement (data/criteria.json, fourkn_merge: 'at least one merged write's COMPARE AND WRITE miscompared and was retried, so the pass exercised the retry') could therefore fail with every correctness check passing.

The cause, instrumented: the row reads the module's merged-write counters on both nodes after the workload and at the end (tests/suite/fourkn_merge.sh:166-169, :208-210; iwr_merge_blocks, iwr_merge_miscompares, iwr_merge_hold_landed, and dbg_iwr_merge_hold_left, what the hold had left). Each VACUOUS lap's reason carries them: all 54 of the record's cells read 'VACUOUS: no swap miscompared in <N> merged writes (hold_landed=<N>), so the row did not exercise the merged write's retry' (tests/suite/fourkn_merge.sh:250-252). The record's evidence quotes 20261022T145928Z_fourkn_merge_2-disk-caw-direct: iwr_merge_blocks 247 and 221, dbg_iwr_merge_hold_left=0 on both nodes, miscompares 0. The holds ran and expired without the peer's write of the held block landing in them: the peer writes a held block only if it happens to be writing that block then.

The fix, one file, tests/suite/fourkn_merge.sh (header :19-42, code :171-207): the workload runs unheld (HOLD_N default 0, :92), and once a lap the overlap is made at the unmount. Each node stats the other's half so the other writes back what it changed (:178-180); node 2 changes its file fb (:181); node 1 is armed to hold its next merged write until the block on the device changes, FORCE_MS (5000) at most (dbg_iwr_merge_hold_n 1, dbg_iwr_merge_hold_peer_ms), changes its file fa in the same inode block and unmounts (:182-186); once the hold has begun (:187) node 2 changes fb again and unmounts (:188), so node 2's swap lands inside node 1's hold and node 1's swap must miscompare and retry. forced=landed requires the hold to have begun, hold_landed and miscompares on node 1 each to have risen (:201-204); a lap whose forced overlap did not land is VACUOUS (:246-249), and fa and fb must read 605 and 606 on both nodes after the remount (:218-221). The knobs restore the row as the fix found it exactly: HOLD_N=8 HOLD_MS=20 HOLD_PEER_MS=1000 hold each node's first 8 merged blocks as before (:142-143, :106-107), and FORCE_MS=0 takes the else branch, the plain unmounts the row made before (:205-207), with every file expected at its writer's round mode (:218).

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: a failing fsx row kept no fsx log in its evidence, so no FAIL of the fsx row could be diagnosed from what the run kept. tests/suite/fsx.sh keeps a failing check's log on the node (/root/fsx.<seed>.<ops>.log, tests/suite/fsx.sh:38; it deletes the log only for a check that passed, :45) and names it in the row's measured text; the fsx row runs through run.sh run_none, which before the fix pulled nothing for a row that did not pass.

A row run by run_none that did not pass (no RESULT line, or a status other than PASS) calls pull_row_artifacts for its node; that pull's selection names fsx.*.log (run.sh:2248, :2250). MXFS_PULL_RUN_NONE=0 skips that pull (:1539), which is exactly the pre-fix path: before the fix run_none had no pull.

The lap: tests/fsx_log_pull_lap.sh runs the fsx row through run.sh with FSX_SEED=-1, so fsx exits with its usage on both checks and the row fails with both logs named (EXPOSED), and passes only if the run's evidence directory holds both logs with fsx's usage text in them.

change.cause: tests/capture_fault_gate.sh ran its entries back to back and never re-formed the pair, so an entry that does not prep the cluster itself started on whatever the previous injected fault left (a node unmounted, without its module, or destroyed) and aborted before its fault line, which the gate read BROKEN; pair_ready now checks the pair before every lap and forms it again (or ends the gate ABORT) when it is not formed

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: capture-gate entries that do not prep the cluster themselves started on the state the previous entry's fault left and aborted before reaching their own fault, so the gate read them BROKEN without measuring them.

The fix, one site: tests/capture_fault_gate.sh pair_ready (:109-:150), called before every fault lap (:151) and healthy lap (:170): each node must answer with /src, the tree's srcversion, the configuration's force_transport and one mxfs mount (pair_formed, :105-:108); a pair that is not formed is powered, waited for and formed again with run.sh prep_cluster, and a pair that cannot be formed ends the gate ABORT. change.cause: tools/batch_lap.py bounded a lap with subprocess.run(timeout=bound), which on expiry ends only the process it started, so a harness's own children outlived the lap and went on writing after it was recorded; run_bounded now starts the lap in a session of its own and on expiry ends the whole process group (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL, 5 s apart) and waits until none of it is left before the lap is recorded

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: tools/batch_lap.py bounded every harness lap with subprocess.run(timeout=bound), which on expiry ends only its direct child. A harness's own children survived the bound and wrote into the lap's log and the evidence the lap is graded from after the lap had been recorded, and while the next lap ran (the record's evidence: control b20261022-8375dc lap 7 recorded at 19:14:48Z with rc=124 while its harness kept writing until 19:15:08Z).

The fix, one site: tools/batch_lap.py run_bounded (:192-232), which main() calls for every lap (:316). The lap runs under Popen(start_new_session=True) (:208-209); on expiry the group gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL, each followed by up to KILL_GRACE_S=5 s (:178-179, :214-226), and the lap is recorded only after proc.wait() with the group gone (:227-232). MXFS_BATCH_LAP_KILLPG=0 (:202-207) runs exactly the pre-fix call, subprocess.run(command, ..., timeout=bound) returning 124 on TimeoutExpired, so the knob takes out the whole fix and nothing else.

The reproducer, tests/batch_lap_killpg_lap.py: it calls batch_lap.run_bounded with a 1 s bound on a harness that starts a child which sleeps 2 s and then appends to a scratch marker, while the harness sleeps 10 s (:36-44, :52-53). EXPOSED is the bound running out with the child alive (rc=124, :55-59); the lap then waits 4 s and FAILs if the marker was written after run_bounded returned (:60-66). The cause is measured directly: in a control lap the child's write lands after the lap was bounded; with the fix the group is ended before the child's 2 s write.

change.cause: tools/release_run.py board_verdict graded the own-rig 2/net/mesh/drbd board without MXFS_OWN_RIG, which that configuration needs to parse and which criteria.py sets only when its own command line names an own-rig configuration, so in the orchestrator no row of the specification applied, the verdict was an empty list, and an empty list read as clean: the DRBD step's second check graded nothing; board_verdict now sets the flag for an own-rig attachment for the duration of the grading and refuses a verdict that graded no row

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: tools/release_run.py board_verdict(candidate, config, board), the orchestrator's own check of a board (step_boards, and the DRBD step's second check of tests/evidence/drbd_rig/criteria.json), returned [] for 2/net/mesh/drbd on candidate 0.90.134 while that board held fio_perf_vs_xfs=SKIP, alloc_witness=FAIL and chk_clean=FAIL (the record's evidence). configuration.parse refuses an own-rig attachment unless MXFS_OWN_RIG=1, which tools/criteria.py sets at import only when its own argv names an own-rig configuration (criteria.py:111); in the orchestrator it is unset, so criteria.applies() matched no row, graded stayed 0, and the empty list was read as a clean board.

The fix, one function, tools/release_run.py board_verdict (:404-431), both hunks behind BOARD_VERDICT_OWN_RIG (:65-69, MXFS_BOARD_VERDICT_OWN_RIG, default on): (a) for an attachment configuration.ATTACHES marks own_rig it sets MXFS_OWN_RIG=1 while it grades and restores the caller's value after (:411-413, :424-428); (b) a verdict that graded no row is returned as a refusal, 'no row of the specification applies at <config>: nothing was graded' (:429-430). With the switch off both hunks are out and the function is the pre-fix one: the flag as its caller has it, and [] returned as clean.

The reproducer, tests/release_board_verdict_lap.py: it computes the board's rows not green for the candidate as an own-rig run sees them (MXFS_OWN_RIG set) and calls release_run.board_verdict in a child process with MXFS_OWN_RIG dropped from its environment and its inputs taken from the environment rather than argv (:34-54, so criteria.py's argv rule cannot set the flag for it, which is what made control b20261022-ec8648 vacuous); EXPOSED when that board has rows not green (:74), PASS when the orchestrator's verdict names the same rows (:76), FAIL otherwise (:78). Hunk (a) is what the lap exercises: with it in, rows are graded and named; with the switch off the verdict is the empty list. Hunk (b) never fires in a fix-on lap, because with (a) in the board's rows are graded; it is the second half of the same fix, refusing the empty verdict the control laps show being read as clean, should any other cause leave no row applying.

FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: tests/suite/fsx.sh ran fsx with its output in /tmp/fsx.$$.<ops>.log, and the script's EXIT trap (rm -rf "$W" /tmp/fsx.$$.*) deleted that log when the script ended, so a check that failed left nothing for run.sh's artifact pull.

The fix, one site, tests/suite/fsx.sh, exactly the saved diff tests/evidence/controls/D-FSX-SH-SENT-FSX-OUTPUT-TO-A-TMP-LOG-ITS-EXIT-TRAP-DELETED.fix.diff (sha256 488a9fbd6b61a4aedc33b6728eaa50a5a0b62ad399606efb762dd9cb3c8326f9): the EXIT trap removes only the work directory, and run_fsx writes /root/fsx.<seed>.<ops>.log, keeps it when fsx exits nonzero and removes it when fsx passes. The same hunk also names the kept log in the row's measured text (fsx_fail_log=) and writes its last lines to the kernel log (mxfs-FSXfail); this removal claims neither, only that the failing check's log survives the row on the node, which is what the lap grades.

The lap, tests/fsx_tmp_log_lap.sh, runs the fsx row through run.sh on a scratch board with FSX_SEED=-1 so both checks fail at once (EXPOSED: the fsx row failed both checks), and passes only when the row's node holds, in /root or /tmp, a file of fsx's usage output written after the lap's mark for each failed check.

The switch MXFS_BATCH_LAP_KILLTREE (tools/batch_lap.py:260) restores exactly the earlier code: subprocess.run(command, ..., timeout=bound).returncode, 124 on TimeoutExpired (:261-265), returning before the subreaper, the new session or the tree kill is reached. The switch MXFS_BATCH_LAP_STALL (tools/batch_lap.py:308) returns outcome, reason and measured unchanged, exactly the earlier recording: the verdict line alone, no stall field. Not gated by the switch, and not claimed by this removal: the --stall option (:348-350) and its one-capture-group check (:357-360), which with the switch off only carry a pattern to stall_graded, and tools/harness_batch.py's pass-through of --stall (:160-161, :470), which this lap does not use.

The lap: tests/batch_lap_stall_lap.py (docstring :1-28) declares a one-lap calibration batch on scratch copies of the queue and the board (MXFS_DEFECTS, MXFS_CRIT), runs tools/batch_lap.py main() on a harness that prints an operation one second over the limit as max_stall_ms=, another half a second longer through '--stall \bop_ms=(\d+)', then RESULT: PASS, and reads the run main() appended to the scratch ledger.
